entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (eIF2B, a translation-initiation factor with recessive missense alleles). Polysomal profiling of knock-in forebrain shows bulk translation is not grossly changed by the mutation.

entries.proposition: For the 33 mRNAs flagged by monosome-versus-polysome distribution and checked by qPCR on several candidates, most were raised in monosome and polysome fractions alike, which the authors read as regulation at transcript level. This sentence does NOT describe the 176 mRNAs with altered polysome association, which the authors read as altered synthesis of the encoded proteins (see the added entry). The paper itself separates the two regimes at the mRNA level for candidates (fraction-resolved qPCR, Fig 1B), so no limitation of polysome-based evidence in general follows from this quote; the restricted claim is only that the 176-mRNA headline does not read the mutant protein.
entries.snippet: We verified the microarray findings for several candidates with qPCR (Fig. 1B). Most mRNAs with altered translation rates were increased in monosome and polysome fractions from 2b5ho mouse brains, indicating that these mRNAs were regulated at transcript level.

entries.snippet: We focused on differences in mRNA levels within the polysome fractions, without taking into account their distribution between monosome and polysome fractions. We identified 176 mRNAs with altered level of polysome association in 2b5ho compared to WT forebrain (115 up and 61 down, Data S3), indicating altered synthesis of the encoded proteins.
